evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.69: imprōvīsum atque inopīnātum (Lewis & Short, s.v. inopīnātus)
terms.comment: Latin says what the surprise is: something unexpected, inopīnātum or imprōvīsum. “Unexpectedly” is ex inopīnātō or ex necopīnātō.
Something to wonder at: mīrum quantum, nec mīrum (see be surprised).
Livy’s word for an unexpected joy or blow.

phrases.latin: sapientī nihil imprōvīsum accidere potest, nihil inopīnātum, nihil omnīnō novum
phrases.english: nothing can come to the wise man unforeseen, nothing unexpected, nothing at all new

sources: Lewis & Short: inopinatus · Lewis & Short: necopinatus · Lewis & Short: mirus · Lewis & Short: improvisus
